title: Try a Lot of Stuff and Keep What Works
coreMove: Run many bounded variations, read the feedback honestly, and keep only what advances the core purpose.
sourcePressure: The sidecar supports disciplined experimentation, institutional learning, variation, feedback, retention, and adaptation in methods without surrendering core identity.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Treating experimentation as random hustle, trend-chasing, or permission to abandon the core whenever a new tactic looks exciting.

sourceAnchors.name: experimentation
sourceAnchors.detail: the source sidecar supports experimentation as part of preserve-the-core and stimulate-progress logic, emphasizing variation, feedback, and retention
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The institution does not have to predict the winning method if it can test many methods and keep the one that proves itself.

tryThisNow: try three ideas and see what works
examples: generic A/B test with button colors

exampleSpecs.domain: urban farmers market testing stall layouts while preserving local-producer standards
exampleSpecs.audience: Emily, market manager with declining Wednesday traffic
exampleSpecs.stakes: vendors need footfall, but the market cannot become a flea market to chase crowds
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Emily chalks three stall patterns over three Wednesdays, counts dwell time and vendor sales, then keeps the layout that helps local produce without adding reseller booths
exampleSpecs.firstImage: chalk arrows drying on wet pavement before vendors arrive

exampleSpecs.domain: physical therapy clinic testing discharge instructions for knee patients
exampleSpecs.audience: Nicolas, clinic owner frustrated by recurring setbacks
exampleSpecs.stakes: patients keep returning with avoidable flare-ups after unclear home routines
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 4:20 p.m., Nicolas compares three instruction formats by follow-up adherence, then keeps the photo card that patients actually use
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three discharge packets lined along a treatment table
mustAvoid: clinician intuition picks the favorite handout

exampleSpecs.domain: public radio station experimenting with local news formats without abandoning public-service reporting
exampleSpecs.audience: Anna, program director watching younger listeners leave
exampleSpecs.stakes: chasing attention could dilute the station's civic role
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "Which pilot made people show up at the council meeting?" Anna asks, then cancels the most popular segment because it did not serve the core
exampleSpecs.firstImage: listener notes beside a council-meeting attendance sheet

exampleSpecs.domain: bike-share maintenance crew testing repair-routing cards across neighborhoods
exampleSpecs.audience: Diego, field operations lead with uneven bike availability
exampleSpecs.stakes: commuters lose trust when docks are full of broken bikes in the same areas
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Diego tapes different routing cards to mechanic vans for two weeks, then keeps the route that reduces repeat broken-bike pickups
exampleSpecs.firstImage: rainwater beading on a laminated van route card

exampleSpecs.domain: language school trying placement interviews, written tests, and trial classes for adult learners
exampleSpecs.audience: Ingrid, academic coordinator defending student confidence
exampleSpecs.stakes: wrong placement makes adults quit before learning begins
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Ingrid one refund report to keep the trial class method and drop the faster written test for borderline students
exampleSpecs.firstImage: refund forms stacked under three placement rubrics

exampleSpecs.domain: specialty pharmacy testing refill reminders for transplant patients under strict adherence rules
exampleSpecs.audience: Lin, pharmacist responsible for missed-dose risk
exampleSpecs.stakes: missed immunosuppressant doses can threaten a transplant
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Lin test phone, postcard, and app reminders on separate refill cohorts, then keep the low-tech call script because it reduces missed pickups
exampleSpecs.firstImage: refill labels sorted into three colored trays

skillTargets: design bounded experiments around the core
choose what to retain after variation

tryThisNowSpec: Write three small variations for one method you use, one measure that tells whether each served the core, and the date you will kill two of them.
sourceAnchorsNote: Frozen source sidecars for this book expose concept support and source artifacts, but little chapter-level anecdote detail after chapter 1. Use only the anchors listed here; do not invent company histories, named executives, studies, or dates.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person direct address, retrospective, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
